title: 5.5 Small Group · Group 2
contentObjective: I can find the volume of a rectangular prism with whole-number edges using length × width × height, explain why the method works, and use it on a problem I have not seen before.

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Filling the School's Time Capsule
revealWordProblem.text: The school is sealing one final time capsule box before burying it. Two donated boxes are available: Box 1 is 7 in long, 4 in wide, and 6 in tall. Box 2 is 8 in long, 5 in wide, and 4 in tall. The class notebook, photos, and mementos need at least 150 cubic inches of space. Find the volume of each box. Do both boxes meet the requirement? If the class wants to waste the least extra space above 150 in³, which box should they choose? Explain your reasoning.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Box 1: V = 7 × 4 × 6 = 168 in³. Box 2: V = 8 × 5 × 4 = 160 in³. Both boxes hold more than 150 in³, so both meet the requirement. Box 1 has 168 − 150 = 18 in³ of extra space, while Box 2 has only 160 − 150 = 10 in³ of extra space. The class should choose Box 2 because it wastes the least space above what is needed.

conceptIntro.heading: Push further — How do we find the volume of a box?
conceptIntro.intro: You already can do this. So we go up a level, not up a number: find what is always true, show it a second way, and be ready to defend it with a reason instead of an answer.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: To find the volume of a box, multiply all three edges: V = length × width × height — and you can say why it is true, and where it would stop being true.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: My time capsule box is 6 long, 4 wide, and 3 tall. I write the formula: V = length × width × height.
I put in the numbers: V = 6 × 4 × 3.
First I multiply two of them: 6 × 4 = 24.
Then I multiply by the last one: 24 × 3 = 72.
So the volume is 72 cubic units. I use cubic units because volume fills space in 3 directions.

explore.instructions: Go deeper: Calculate the volume of each time capsule container. Use V = l × w × h. As you work, ask yourself WHY it works.

onLevel.stem: Two storage bins: Bin A is 8 × 6 × 5 inches. Bin B is 9 × 4 × 7 inches. Which holds more and by how much?
onLevel.explanation: Bin A: 8 × 6 × 5 = 240 in³. Bin B: 9 × 4 × 7 = 252 in³. Bin B holds 12 in³ more.
choiceFeedback: Calculate both volumes first: Bin A = 8 × 6 × 5 and Bin B = 9 × 4 × 7.
Which bin has the larger volume? Find the difference.
Check your arithmetic: 8 × 6 × 5 = ? and 9 × 4 × 7 = ?
hints: This is a two-part question: which bin holds more AND by how many cubic inches. You need both volumes first.
Find each volume with V = l × w × h, then subtract the smaller total from the larger to get the difference.
Start with Bin A: 8 × 6 = 48, then × 5. Next do Bin B: 9 × 4 = 36, then × 7. Compare the totals.
onLevel.stemEs: Dos cajas de almacenamiento: la Caja A mide 8 × 6 × 5 pulgadas. La Caja B mide 9 × 4 × 7 pulgadas. ¿Cuál guarda más y por cuánto?
onLevel.explanationEs: Caja A: 8 × 6 × 5 = 240 in³. Caja B: 9 × 4 × 7 = 252 in³. La Caja B guarda 12 in³ más.
hintsEs: Esta pregunta tiene dos partes: cuál caja guarda más Y por cuántas pulgadas cúbicas. Necesitas ambos volúmenes primero.
Halla cada volumen con V = l × a × h y luego resta el total menor del mayor para obtener la diferencia.
Empieza con la Caja A: 8 × 6 = 48 y luego × 5. Después la Caja B: 9 × 4 = 36 y luego × 7. Compara los totales.

onLevel.title: Added the Last Edge

workedExample.label: Dimensions
workedExample.work: A capsule is 6 long, 5 wide, and 3 tall
workedExample.workEs: Una cápsula mide 6 de largo, 5 de ancho y 3 de alto

onLevel.correctWork: The student multiplied the first two edges correctly (6 × 5 = 30) but then added the height instead of multiplying it. Every edge must be multiplied: V = 6 × 5 × 3 = 90 cubic units.
hints: Look at the Calculate step. Was the height added or multiplied?
Multiply all three edges: 6 × 5 × 3 = 90 cubic units, not 6 × 5 + 3 = 33.
onLevel.explanation: The Calculate step starts fine with 6 × 5 = 30, but then the student writes + 3 instead of × 3, landing on 33. Volume multiplies every edge, so the correct work is V = 6 × 5 × 3 = 90 cubic units.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso Calcular empieza bien con 6 × 5 = 30, pero luego el estudiante escribe + 3 en lugar de × 3 y llega a 33. El volumen multiplica todas las aristas, así que el trabajo correcto es V = 6 × 5 × 3 = 90 unidades cúbicas.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: El estudiante multiplicó bien las dos primeras aristas (6 × 5 = 30) pero luego sumó el alto en lugar de multiplicarlo. Todas las aristas se multiplican: V = 6 × 5 × 3 = 90 unidades cúbicas.

onLevel.stem: A rectangular prism has length 8 cm, width 5 cm, and height 4 cm. What is its volume?
choiceFeedback: Are you adding the dimensions? Volume multiplies all edges: length × width × height.
Multiply only two dimensions? All three must be multiplied: 8 × 5 × 4.
Check your multiplication: 8 × 5 = 40, then 40 × 4 = ?
hints: The prism's edges are 8 cm, 5 cm, and 4 cm. Volume means multiplying those edges, not adding them.
Apply V = l × w × h with all three numbers — leaving one out gives an area, not a volume.
Multiply 8 × 5 = 40 first, then multiply that result by the height, 4 cm.
onLevel.stemEs: Un prisma rectangular tiene largo 8 cm, ancho 5 cm y altura 4 cm. ¿Cuál es su volumen?
hintsEs: Las aristas del prisma son 8 cm, 5 cm y 4 cm. El volumen significa multiplicar esas aristas, no sumarlas.
Aplica V = l × a × h con los tres números: dejar uno fuera da un área, no un volumen.
Multiplica 8 × 5 = 40 primero y luego multiplica ese resultado por la altura, 4 cm.

onLevel.stem: A box has a volume of 72 in³. Its base is 6 in by 4 in. What is its height?
choiceFeedback: Multiply the dimensions instead of dividing? Use 72 ÷ (6 × 4).
Find 6 × 4 first, then divide 72 by that result.
Double-check: height × 24 = 72. What is height?
hints: You know the volume (72 in³) and the base (6 in by 4 in). Only the height is unknown.
Since volume = base area × height, divide the volume by the base area to work backward to the height.
First compute the base area: 6 × 4 = 24 in². Then ask: 24 times what equals 72?
onLevel.stemEs: Una caja tiene un volumen de 72 in³. Su base mide 6 in por 4 in. ¿Cuál es su altura?

extending.title: Find the Volume Error

workedExample.label: Dimensions
workedExample.work: l = 9 ft, w = 4 ft, h = 6 ft
workedExample.workEs: l = 9 pies, a = 4 pies, h = 6 pies

extending.correctWork: 4 × 6 = 24, not 10. The student added instead of multiplied. Correct: V = 9 × 24 = 216 ft³.
hints: Check Step 3: what is 4 × 6?
4 × 6 = 24, not 10. The student added 4 + 6 instead of multiplying.
extending.explanation: Inside the Calculate step the student replaced 4 × 6 with 10, which is 4 + 6. Multiplying gives 4 × 6 = 24, so the volume is V = 9 × 24 = 216 ft³, not 90 ft³.
extending.explanationEs: Dentro del paso Calcular, el estudiante cambió 4 × 6 por 10, que en realidad es 4 + 6. Al multiplicar se obtiene 4 × 6 = 24, así que el volumen es V = 9 × 24 = 216 ft³, no 90 ft³.
extending.correctWorkEs: 4 × 6 = 24, no 10. El estudiante sumó en lugar de multiplicar. Correcto: V = 9 × 24 = 216 ft³.

extending.prompt: A box needs to hold exactly 60 cubic inches. Give three different sets of whole-number dimensions that work. Which set would make the box closest to a cube shape? Why might that matter?
extending.sentenceFrame: Option 1: ___ × ___ × ___. Option 2: ___ × ___ × ___. Option 3: ___ × ___ × ___. The ___ option is closest to a cube because ___. This matters because ___.
extending.hint: Find three different factor combinations of the target volume.
hints: You need three DIFFERENT whole-number triples that multiply to exactly 60, like l × w × h = 60.
Start with a factor pair of 60 (like 6 × 10), then split one factor into two numbers to make a triple.
Try 60 = 6 × 10, then break the 10 into 2 × 5 for one triple. Then hunt for triples whose numbers are closer to equal.
extending.explanation: Any three whole numbers whose product is 60 work, such as 1 × 6 × 10, 2 × 5 × 6, and 3 × 4 × 5. Of those, 3 × 4 × 5 is closest to a cube because its edges are nearest to equal, and a cube-like box uses less material for its surface while holding the same 60 cubic inches.
extending.explanationEs: Sirve cualquier trío de números enteros cuyo producto sea 60, como 1 × 6 × 10, 2 × 5 × 6 y 3 × 4 × 5. De esos, 3 × 4 × 5 es el más parecido a un cubo porque sus aristas son las más cercanas entre sí, y una caja parecida a un cubo usa menos material en su superficie aunque guarde las mismas 60 pulgadas cúbicas.
extending.promptEs: Una caja debe contener exactamente 60 pulgadas cúbicas. Da tres conjuntos distintos de dimensiones con números enteros que funcionen. ¿Cuál conjunto haría la caja más parecida a un cubo? ¿Por qué podría importar eso?
hintsEs: Necesitas tres tríos DIFERENTES de números enteros que multiplicados den exactamente 60, o sea l × a × h = 60.
Empieza con una pareja de factores de 60 (como 6 × 10) y luego parte un factor en dos números para formar un trío.
Prueba 60 = 6 × 10 y luego parte el 10 en 2 × 5 para un trío. Después busca tríos cuyos números sean más parecidos entre sí.

extending.stem: A shipping crate is 12 ft long, 3 ft wide, and 2 ft tall. How many 1-foot cubes exactly fill it?
extending.explanation: The number of unit cubes equals the volume: 12 × 3 × 2 = 72 cubes.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. The number of unit cubes equals the volume: 12 × 3 × 2 = ___ cubes.
Add dimensions or divide incorrectly? The volume (12 × 3 × 2) equals unit cubes.
Verify: 12 × 3 = 36, then 36 × 2 = ? cubes.
hints: Each 1-foot cube takes up exactly 1 ft³, so the number of cubes equals the crate's volume in cubic feet.
Find the crate's volume with V = l × w × h — that total IS the number of unit cubes that fit.
Start with one layer: 12 × 3 = 36 cubes. Then multiply by the height, 2 ft, for the number of layers.
extending.stemEs: Una caja de envío mide 12 ft de largo, 3 ft de ancho y 2 ft de alto. ¿Cuántos cubos de 1 pie la llenan exactamente?
extending.explanationEs: La cantidad de cubos unitarios es igual al volumen: 12 × 3 × 2 = 72 cubos.
hintsEs: Cada cubo de 1 pie ocupa exactamente 1 pie³, así que el número de cubos es igual al volumen del cajón en pies cúbicos.
Halla el volumen del cajón con V = l × a × h: ese total ES el número de cubos unitarios que caben.
Empieza con una capa: 12 × 3 = 36 cubos. Luego multiplica por la altura, 2 pies, para el número de capas.

extending.stem: Two prisms have the same volume of 48 cm³. Prism A is 4 × 4 × 3. Prism B is 8 × 3 × h. What is h?
extending.explanation: Prism A volume = 4 × 4 × 3 = 48 cm³. For Prism B, h = 48 ÷ (8 × 3) = 48 ÷ 24 = 2 cm.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Prism A volume = 4 × 4 × 3 = 48 cm³.
Use the formula: h = Volume ÷ (length × width).
Verify: 8 × 3 × h = 48. What value of h works?
hints: Both prisms hold 48 cm³. Prism B gives you two edges (8 and 3) and hides the height h.
Use h = Volume ÷ (length × width): divide 48 by the product of Prism B's two known edges.
Multiply 8 × 3 = 24 first. Then find what number times 24 equals 48.
extending.stemEs: Dos prismas tienen el mismo volumen de 48 cm³. El Prisma A mide 4 × 4 × 3. El Prisma B mide 8 × 3 × h. ¿Cuánto vale h?
extending.explanationEs: Volumen del Prisma A = 4 × 4 × 3 = 48 cm³. Para el Prisma B, h = 48 ÷ (8 × 3) = 48 ÷ 24 = 2 cm.

extending.stem: A time capsule box is 5 units long, 3 units wide, and 2 units tall. How many unit cubes fill it?
extending.explanation: V = length × width × height = 5 × 3 × 2 = 30 cubic units.
choiceFeedback: Add the three dimensions, not multiply them. How many cubes fill the entire box?
Did you include all three dimensions? You need length × width × height.
Try multiplying the three dimensions in the order: length × width × height.
extending.stemEs: Una caja de cápsula del tiempo mide 5 unidades de largo, 3 unidades de ancho y 2 unidades de alto. ¿Cuántos cubos unitarios la llenan?
extending.explanationEs: V = largo × ancho × altura = 5 × 3 × 2 = 30 unidades cúbicas.
hints: Volume counts how many unit cubes fit inside a solid, so the answer will be in cubic units.
Use V = length × width × height and put all three given measurements into that formula.
Start with the bottom layer: 5 × 3 = 15 cubes in one layer. Now use the height to finish.
hintsEs: El volumen cuenta cuántos cubos unitarios caben dentro de un cuerpo, así que la respuesta irá en unidades cúbicas.
Usa V = largo × ancho × altura y coloca las tres medidas dadas en esa fórmula.
Comienza con la capa de abajo: 5 × 3 = 15 cubos en una capa. Ahora usa la altura para terminar.

extending.stem: You stack unit cubes in a capsule: each layer has 6 cubes, and there are 4 layers. What is the volume?
extending.explanation: Each layer has 6 cubes and there are 4 layers, so 6 × 4 = 24 cubic units. This is the same as length × width × height with one factor being the number of layers.
choiceFeedback: Add the cubes per layer and the layers, not multiply. Try 6 × 4.
Count how many cubes per layer, then multiply by the number of layers.
Recount: 6 cubes per layer times 4 layers equals how many total?
extending.stemEs: Apilas cubos unitarios en una cápsula: cada capa tiene 6 cubos y hay 4 capas. ¿Cuál es el volumen?
extending.explanationEs: Cada capa tiene 6 cubos y hay 4 capas, así que 6 × 4 = 24 unidades cúbicas. Esto es lo mismo que largo × ancho × altura, donde uno de los factores es la cantidad de capas.
hints: Volume is the total number of unit cubes inside, no matter how they are grouped.
When cubes are stacked in identical layers, multiply the cubes in one layer by the number of layers.
One layer holds 6 cubes, so two layers hold 12. Keep going until you have accounted for all 4 layers.
hintsEs: El volumen es la cantidad total de cubos unitarios que hay dentro, sin importar cómo estén agrupados.
Cuando los cubos están apilados en capas idénticas, multiplica los cubos de una capa por el número de capas.
Una capa tiene 6 cubos, así que dos capas tienen 12. Sigue así hasta considerar las 4 capas.

workedExample.label: Dimensions
workedExample.work: A capsule is 5 long, 3 wide, and 4 tall
workedExample.workEs: Una cápsula mide 5 de largo, 3 de ancho y 4 de alto

extending.correctWork: The student added the edges instead of multiplying. Volume = 5 × 3 × 4 = 60 cubic units. Adding the edges (5 + 3 + 4 = 12) does not count the cubes that fill the box.
hints: Look at the Calculate step. Should the three edges be added or multiplied?
Volume multiplies the edges: 5 × 3 × 4 = 60 cubic units, not 5 + 3 + 4 = 12.
extending.titleEs: Extensión Nivel 2 — Error al apilar cubos
extending.explanation: In the Calculate step the student wrote 5 + 3 + 4 = 12, adding the edges instead of multiplying them. Adding only walks along three edges; filling the box takes 5 × 3 × 4 = 60 cubic units.
extending.explanationEs: En el paso Calcular, el estudiante escribió 5 + 3 + 4 = 12, sumando las aristas en lugar de multiplicarlas. Sumar solo recorre tres aristas; llenar la caja requiere 5 × 3 × 4 = 60 unidades cúbicas.
extending.correctWorkEs: El estudiante sumó las aristas en lugar de multiplicarlas. Volumen = 5 × 3 × 4 = 60 unidades cúbicas. Sumar las aristas (5 + 3 + 4 = 12) no cuenta los cubos que llenan la caja.

extending.stem: What is the volume of a rectangular prism with l = 7 in, w = 3 in, h = 4 in?
extending.explanation: V = l × w × h = 7 × 3 × 4 = 84 cubic inches.
choiceFeedback: Add 7 + 3 instead of multiplying? Volume uses multiplication of all three edges.
Square inches (in²) measure area, not volume. Volume is cubic (in³).
Multiply all three dimensions: 7 × 3 × 4, not 7 × 3 ÷ 2.
hints: Notice the three edge lengths: l = 7 in, w = 3 in, h = 4 in. Volume asks how much space fills the whole box.
Use the volume formula V = l × w × h, and remember volume is measured in cubic units (in³).
Start with 7 × 3 = 21 for the base, then multiply that result by the height, 4 inches.
extending.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el volumen de un prisma rectangular con l = 7 in, w = 3 in, h = 4 in?
extending.explanationEs: V = l × w × h = 7 × 3 × 4 = 84 pulgadas cúbicas.
hintsEs: Fíjate en las tres aristas: l = 7 pulg, a = 3 pulg, h = 4 pulg. El volumen pregunta cuánto espacio llena toda la caja.
Usa la fórmula del volumen V = l × a × h, y recuerda que el volumen se mide en unidades cúbicas (pulg³).
Empieza con 7 × 3 = 21 para la base y luego multiplica ese resultado por la altura, 4 pulgadas.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Volume with Whole Number Edges is multiplying only two of the three edges and stopping there — for example, seeing a box that is 6 in long, 4 in wide, and 3 in tall, multiplying just 6 × 4 = 24, and calling that the volume, when 24 is only the area of the bottom face (in square inches), not the volume of the whole box. The height must also be multiplied in: V = 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 cubic inches. A second common mistake is adding the three edges instead of multiplying them (6 + 4 + 3 = 13 instead of 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 cubic inches). Volume always MULTIPLIES all three edges, and the answer is always labeled in cubic units (in³), never square units (in²) or plain units (in).

check.stem: What is the volume of the large box?
check.explanation: V = l × w × h = 24 × 18 × 18 = 7,776 cubic inches.

check.stem: What is the volume of the medium box?
How many more cubic inches does the large box hold?

connect.modelAnswer: Large box: V = 24 × 18 × 18 = 7,776 in³. Medium box: V = 18 × 14 × 12 = 3,024 in³. The large box holds 7,776 − 3,024 = 4,752 more cubic inches.

exitTicket.stem: Explain your thinking — A rectangular prism has l = 11 in, w = 5 in, h = 4 in. What is the volume?
exitTicket.explanation: V = 11 × 5 × 4 = 220 cubic inches. Remember: volume uses cubic units (in³).
choiceFeedback: Multiply all three edges: 11 × 5 = 55, then 55 × 4 = ?
Square inches (in²) measure area, not volume. Volume uses cubic units (in³).
Did you calculate 11 × 5 × 4 correctly?
hints: Note the three edges: l = 11 in, w = 5 in, h = 4 in — and watch the units, since volume is cubic (in³).
Use V = l × w × h, multiplying all three edges together, and pick an answer with cubic units.
Multiply 11 × 5 = 55 first, then multiply that result by the height, 4 inches.

questions.stem: A rectangle has vertices at (1, 1), (5, 1), (5, 4), (1, 4). What is its perimeter?
What is the distance between (-4, 3) and (2, 3)?
questions.explanation: Both points have y = 3, so this is a horizontal distance. |2 - (-4)| = |2 + 4| = 6 units.

questions.stem: What is the distance between (5, -2) and (5, 4)?
questions.explanation: Both points have x = 5, so this is a vertical distance. |4 - (-2)| = |4 + 2| = 6 units.

parallelPractice.stem: A composite figure has rectangles 6×3 and 2×3. Find the total area.
hints: Re-read the question. What exactly is it asking you to find?
Use the visual model, then complete one step at a time.
Start like this: First rectangle: 6 × 3 = 18.
parallelPractice.explanation: First rectangle: 6 × 3 = 18. Second rectangle: 2 × 3 = 6. Add both areas: 24.
parallelPractice.stemEs: Una figura compuesta tiene rectángulos 6×3 y 2×3. Encuentra el área total.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer la pregunta. ¿Qué te pide encontrar exactamente?
Usa el modelo visual y completa un paso a la vez.
Empieza así: Primer rectángulo: 6 × 3 = 18.
parallelPractice.explanationEs: Primer rectángulo: 6 × 3 = 18. Segundo rectángulo: 2 × 3 = 6. Suma las dos áreas: 24.
